subject: Critical: CedarPoint elevated error rate / throughput spike — status & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@cedarpoint.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Marie Collins <marie.collins@cedarpoint.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: elevated error-rate and 503s on /generate

Avery —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 503s and timeouts against the /generate endpoints at ~07:50 PT. Error rate climbed from ~0.4% to ~6% and p95 latency jumped from 220ms to >2.5s. This is impacting checkouts on our webhook flow and a subset of real-time personalization calls.

Attached is a quick heatmap from our side (cedarpoint_error_map.png). We have a rolling mitigation (retries + backoff) in place but customers are seeing failures. Can you confirm if this is on Redwood infrastructure or a configuration change on our end? We need a clear ETA and whether you will open a support escalation with exec attention.

Ben
Product Ops | CedarPoint
ben.thomas@cedarpoint.com

Attachment: cedarpoint_error_map.png (image/png, 372KB)

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: elevated error-rate and 503s on /generate

Team —

Thanks for the heads up, Ben. I’m pulling ops and infra into this thread. Initial read from monitoring: a shard of the N. Virginia cluster entered a degraded state around 07:46 due to elevated queue depth during a short traffic spike. That propagated to fallbacks and increased contention on the KV cache which magnified latencies.

Immediate actions we are starting now (T-0):
- David/Kim: scale the affected GPU shard by +2 nodes and enable aggressive prefetch for KV (5–10 min expected to take effect).
- Monica: flip routing policy to route CedarPoint traffic to secondary pool in the eu-west standby (safe cross-region fallback) for low-latency critical flows — will keep non-critical jobs throttled.
- Sergio: open an ops bridge and post link; start collecting sample request ids for cherry-pick tracing.

I’m drafting a short exec note to send to CedarPoint leadership with ETA and mitigation plan. Monica, please attach the mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf we used last quarter and include the rollback path.

Avery
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 1.1MB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: elevated error-rate and 503s on /generate — infra findings

Quick technical summary after first pass:
- Root cause (probable): autoscaler lag + KV cache thrashing when a high-fanout batch job hit within a 90s window. The metrics show sustained GPU utilization ~98% on shard-nv-3 and 30–40% queuing in the scheduler.
- Short-term mitigation completed: added 2 x p4d nodes to shard-nv-3 (expected capacity up in ~6min), switched CedarPoint route to standby pool for latency-critical endpoints only.
- Additional steps (pending exec approval): bring up emergency reserved pool (dedicated capacity) for CedarPoint for the next 24 hours to stabilize traffic while we root-cause and tune batch schedules. Cost and contract exceptions will need signoff.

Kimberly — can you confirm if sales/legal are comfortable with a one-day reserved pool and draft a quick customer credit offer? Monica — please confirm the cross-region routing telemetry once live.

I’ll keep this thread updated with telemetry screenshots and request ids.

—David
VP, Infrastructure

Attachment: telemetry_snapshot_0903.png (image/png, 280KB)

From: Marie Collins <marie.collins@cedarpoint.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@cedarpoint.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: elevated error-rate and 503s on /generate

Avery —

Thanks for the immediate actions and for pulling in infra. Two asks from our side: 1) Can you give an ETA for when error rate will be back below 1% for our high-priority checkout flow? 2) Please include the bridge link and a clear point of contact — our CEO is looped on high-impact incidents and wants to be briefed if this is >2 hours.

We appreciate the cross-region routing but need confirmation on data residency for requests routed to eu-west (are payloads persisted in-region?). If there’s any need for a reserved pool we are open to a short-term commitment if it reduces customer impact.

On a separate note — I’m pasting the snippet from Ben’s original note for context:

> On Sat, Sep 23, 2028 at 08:12 Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@cedarpoint.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp uptick in 503s and timeouts against the /generate endpoints at ~07:50 PT. Error rate climbed from ~0.4% to ~6% and p95 latency jumped from 220ms to >2.5s.

Marie

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@cedarpoint.com>, Marie Collins <marie.collins@cedarpoint.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Critical: CedarPoint elevated error rate / throughput spike — status & next steps

Team / CedarPoint execs — final update from today’s stabilization window and next steps: 

What we saw (summary):
- Short, high-fanout batch created scheduler queue pressure at 07:46 PT. One shard (shard-nv-3) hit sustained 95–99% GPU utilization which led to KV cache pressure and higher tail latency. Impact window: ~07:46–08:10 PT.

Immediate mitigations completed (by 09:05 PT):
- +2 p4d nodes added to shard-nv-3; autoscaler tuned to react faster to queue depth spikes.
- CedarPoint high-priority endpoints re-routed to standby pool with pre-warmed capacity; non-critical flows throttled.
- Telemetry capture and request-id collection done; we have sample traces for root-cause repro.

Customer impact & ETA:
- Observed error rate returned to ~0.8% for the checkout flow by 09:12 PT; p95 latency back under 300ms for routed traffic. We will continue monitoring for 48 hours.

Decision made (exec level):
- Spin up a 24-hour reserved pool (emergency dedicated capacity) for CedarPoint starting immediately to eliminate autoscaler tail risk while we complete tuning. Expected live time: within 30 minutes of approval. Kimberly is preparing the order and quick credit proposal; finance cadence required for >$X/day spend.

Owners and next steps:
- David Kim: full root-cause analysis and KV cache tuning (deliverable: RCA draft within 48 hours).
- Monica Patel: monitor cross-region routing telemetry and confirm data residency behavior (deliverable: confirmation within 4 hours).
- Kimberly Park: customer credit wording and finance signoff (deliverable: pricing note in 2 hours).
- Sergio Alvarez: maintain ops bridge and run continuous sampling until SLA stable (ops bridge: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/OPS-bridge-cedarpoint).

We will send a concise customer-facing incident summary and a follow-up RCA. Thank you CedarPoint team for the quick coordination. I’ll keep this channel open and update every 2 hours until we hand back to standard cadence.

Avery Johnson
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf, telemetry_snapshot_0903.png
